portfolio_warnings: There were no exact matches in any individual fingerprint field across the permitted candidate-history comparisons; every review therefore records all six fields as changed, and semantic classification does not imply literal equality.

The three fresh CBAM candidates are all adjacent to the historical CBAM desk and to one another. None brings a signed broker route, demonstrated supplier-data access, or a conservative above-threshold customer denominator, so researching all three would duplicate the same unresolved gate.

Several renewable and installer-channel candidates remain adjacent to BatteryFit or the heat-pump commissioning passport. Family-company pilot access is useful for proof but is not a scalable distribution contract, an approval right, or protection from OEM and installer bundling.

Many candidates turn a regulation into a checklist, evidence pack, register, or monitor. A compulsory rule creates urgency but not defensibility when free official tools, trusted professionals, ERP or QMS vendors, and capable AI users can reproduce the deliverable.

Most discovery economics fields are still unset. Historical proximity cannot substitute for bottom-up customer counts, sustainable prices, delivery margins, founder time, or a plausible founder wealth path.

Partner embedding is repeatedly asserted for brokers, converters, accounting offices, insurers, lessors, service firms, and software vendors. Until written access and routed paid cases exist, these are third-party gates rather than compounding distribution.

A materially-different label means that payer, trigger, offer, distribution, or control structure genuinely changed; it is not validation. Historical labels and scores were used only to locate provenance and terminal objections, not as current evidence.
